title: Elementary changes between generating tuples over a local ring
statement: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative unital local ring (a ring with a unique maximal ideal), with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $M$ be a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (a module generated by a finite set), and let $c\geq0$. If $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$ are ordered generating tuples for $M$, then one can transform $f$ into $g$ by a finite sequence of the following invertible operations: multiply one entry by a unit of $R$; interchange two entries; replace one entry $f_i$ by $f_i+a f_j$, where $a\in R$ and $i\ne j$. Equivalently there is a matrix $P\in\mathrm{GL}_c(R)$ with $g=Pf$, and $P$ can be chosen as a product of matrices of these three types. No freeness, independence, regular-sequence, principal-ideal-domain, or minimality hypothesis on the tuples is imposed. In particular this applies to an ideal generated by $c$ elements, viewed as a finite $R$-module. The empty tuple case says $M=0$ and uses no operations.
